Verified on throwaway PORT=8090 (never touched the shared :80 instance): loopback caller + real 1x1 png under the temp root -> 200/image/png/68 bytes. Same request from this machines LAN address 192.168.1.206 -> 403. Loopback caller with a `..` traversal (Temp\..\..\..\evil.png, resolves to C:\Users\mike\evil.png, outside root) -> 403, proving the confinement check fires before the existsSync 404 would. assign.now: wiring the shots wall into ext/AITask

log.msg: End-to-end demo: took 5 real screenshots via mcp__site__shot against the live :80 server (localhost/framework/ai/ at 1400x1000 and 390x844, /framework/ext/AITask/, /framework/ext/JSONL/, /framework/ at 3440x1440) -- confirmed real PNGs on disk at their exact requested dimensions (file(1)/magic-byte check). Appended 5 `shot` lines to this task's own task.jsonl. First attempt broke JSON: printf turned a Windows path separator into a bare backslash before a letter, which JSON rejects (ext/JSONL readme's own documented trap) -- caught by JSON.parse-ing every line by hand, fixed by switching the path field to forward slashes (Node/Windows accept either; path.resolve() confirmed it still lands inside the guarded root). Headless Playwright probe against the throwaway PORT=8090 instance (has Screenshots.js): all 5 .ai-shot render, naturalWidth on each exactly matches its PNG's real width (1400/1400/1400/390/3440), complete:true, 0 console errors, click targets are the real /screenshot?path=... urls. Second probe against the LIVE shared :80 server (Screenshots.js NOT registered there -- needs a restart) hitting the same task page: all 5 render .missing, fallback swatch visible (display:flex), hidden (display:none), 0 console errors, 0 failed requests logged -- the graceful-degradation path fires correctly for exactly the case Mike flagged (route not live until a restart). Off-localhost (true static hosting) is the simpler case -- LOCAL is false so shots.js never creates the at all -- verified by code inspection against the same LOCAL pattern feed.js already uses, not a live test.

Design question, answered: chose the explicit `shot` log line over scraping the session transcript. One sentence why: the transcript is a format ext/JSONL does not own and can change under us with any Claude Code update, where a log line is a contract this repo controls end to end -- and RULE#18 (minimize the chaos) favors the smaller, obvious mechanism (one verb, one array, ~25 lines of render code) over a parser that would have to find image tool_results inside `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl`, decide which ones are screenshots vs pasted images, and re-derive a url/width/label nothing in the transcript actually states. What scraping would have bought: zero-effort capture -- a worker that forgets to log still shows up -- at the cost of coupling the dashboard to a transcript shape ext/AITask already treats as read-only and dev-only (AILogs.js), and no way to attach the label/width/future scores a log line carries for free.

Dashboard url: http://localhost/framework/ai/2026-08-17/shots-in-log/ -- shows the Screenshots wall with 5 real thumbnails, 1400/1400/1400/390/3440 wide, clickable to full size, once the shared :80 server is restarted to pick up Server/plugins/Screenshots.js (confirmed live already on the throwaway :8090 instance in this run -- see the end-to-end demo log line). Until that restart the same url renders correctly today, right now: the graceful-degradation swatches, verified moments ago against the actual live :80 server with 0 console errors.

assign.outcome: **Screenshots taken outside the repo now show up in the AI task log dashboard.** Dashboard url: http://localhost/framework/ai/2026-08-17/shots-in-log/ (real thumbnails once the shared :80 server restarts to pick up the new plugin; graceful placeholders there right now, verified). **The convention** — ext/JSONL's new `shot` verb, documented in ext/JSONL/readme.md: `{"shot": {"at", "path" (absolute), "url", "width", "label"}}`. Deliberately just a dict — a `scores` object arrives later with no shape change. **Design choice, as asked:** an explicit log line, not transcript-scraping — a log line is a contract this repo owns end to end, where the transcript is a format ext/JSONL does not own and could change under us; RULE#18 also favors the smaller mechanism (one verb, ~25 lines of render code) over a parser that would have to infer which transcript images are screenshots. What scraping would have bought: capture with nothing to remember — a worker that forgets the log line still shows up. **The guard, born on, not added later:** `Server/plugins/Screenshots.js` reuses `loopback()` from MCP.js (same as AILogs.js/SocketServer.js) and confines the requested path to `os.tmpdir()` *after* `path.resolve()`. Verified on a throwaway PORT=8090 instance, the shared :80 server never touched or restarted: loopback + real png -> 200/image/png at the exact byte count; the same request from this machine's LAN address (192.168.1.206) -> 403; a `..` traversal that resolves outside the root -> 403 (fires before the 404 a missing file would give). Recorded in Server/README.md beside the AILogs.js entry. **Graceful degradation, verified two ways:** off `localhost`, `shots.js` never creates an `` element at all (code parity with feed.js's existing LOCAL check — no live test of true static hosting). On `localhost` without the route live yet — the exact state of the shared :80 server right now — a headless Playwright probe confirmed all 5 real shots render `.missing` with the fallback swatch shown, the `` hidden, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests. **End-to-end demo:** 5 real screenshots taken via `mcp__site__shot` against the live :80 server (/framework/ai/ at 1400x1000 and 390x844, /framework/ext/AITask/, /framework/ext/JSONL/, /framework/ at 3440x1440), confirmed real PNGs at their exact requested dimensions, logged as `shot` lines in this task's own task.jsonl, and confirmed rendering on the guarded throwaway instance — each thumbnail's `naturalWidth` matched its PNG exactly. **Hit and fixed the exact trap ext/JSONL's readme documents:** a shell-escaping slip put a bare backslash before a letter in a `path` field, which JSON rejects — caught by JSON-parsing every line by hand rather than trusting the append, fixed with forward slashes (Windows/Node accept either). **Docs:** ext/JSONL/readme.md + doc/task-jsonl.md + doc/file/JSONL.js.md + page.js (the convention); ext/AITask/readme.md + doc/manifest.md + doc/file/ai.css.md + new doc/method/shots.md + doc/file/shots.js.md + page.js's methods:/files: lists (the renderer). Cross-checked files:/methods: lists against disk — no orphans, nothing missing. Headless-checked the touched doc pages: 0 console errors, 0 .md-error boxes, 0 horizontal overflow (one pre-existing, unrelated 404 on every files// page confirmed on an untouched file too, not introduced here). **Deliberately left for later** (matches the brief's own scope): server-side thumbnail generation (would need an image-processing dependency, LAW#4) — today's thumbnail is the full-resolution PNG sized down by CSS, with lazy-loading doing the real work of keeping 100 logged shots from costing 100 requests up front. The scoring layer (layout/contrast/density ratings) the brief explicitly defers. Token spend below is bounded to lines timestamped at/after this task's `requested_at` in the session transcript, which only caught 5 of this run's many tool calls (the transcript file lagged the live conversation) — a floor, not the true figure; the window fractions are the reliable number.
